O.outcome_detail: P200 amplitude during even- versus odd-position digit encoding

cells.quote: More importantly, we found the interaction effect of Position × Session, F (1, 15) = 3.79, p < 0.05, η2 partial = 0.17: the post-training session showed greater P200 amplitude in response to even-position digits (3.08 ± 0.96 μV) compared to odd-position digits (1.34 ± 0.80 μV), p < 0.05 (Fig. 4). No other main effect or interaction was signiﬁcant. As a control, in the NC group, there was no such P200 effect, as indicated by the lack of signiﬁcance for the effects involving Session or Position, all ps > 0.41.
cells.note: The study interpreted the trained odd-even P200 pattern as an encoding-pattern change.

O.outcome_detail: left-anterior theta power during even- versus odd-position digit encoding

cells.quote: Importantly, there was a signi ﬁcant three-way interaction, F (2, 30) = 6.92, p < 0.05, η2 partial = 0.37. Breaking down the ANOVA based on the factor Session revealed an interaction between Position and Area for the post-training session, F (2, 30) = 14.43, p < 0.01, η2 partial = 0.55. Further analysis showed that the post-training session demonstrated a signi ﬁcant increase in theta power from the odd- (10 ± 5 %, percent signal change) to even-position (24 ± 6 %) condition in the left anterior area, p < 0.05 (Fig. 5), but the pre-training session did not. No other main effect or interaction was signi ﬁcant. In the NC group, the three-way ANOVA found no signi ﬁcant results, all ps > 0.09.
cells.note: The study interpreted the theta odd-even pattern as a trained encoding-pattern change.

O.outcome_detail: number-noun pairs episodic-memory accuracy at follow-up

result.effect: significant Group × Session interaction; effect size not reported

cells.quote: After applying false-discovery-rate (FDR) corrections to all resulting p values, we observed a signi ﬁcant interaction effect on the number-noun pairs measure, suggesting that the MT group performed better on this test compared to the NC group after undergoing training and the improvement persisted over time as seen in the follow-up (Table 1). No other signi ﬁcant interaction effects were observed.
cells.note: Follow-up testing occurred 4 months after training; the study does not report the interaction's printed test statistic or effect size in the supplied text.
